problems.statement: The forced move from downtown Castellan Hall (2,150 seats, by rail) to the distant, smaller Brightwater venue (1,290 seats, poor transit) is the main driver of the ticket-revenue drop, through lost access and lost capacity.
The music director's programming (more post-1945 works and commissions) is driving audiences away.
Marketing is invisible and ineffective, and this explains the decline.
Marketing and communications is not the music director's responsibility, so it cannot be a ground for judging her contract.

A region-wide secular decline (ageing subscribers, cost of living, post-2020 habits) accounts for part of the fall, and the venue effect cannot yet be separated from it. Peers fell a similar cumulative amount without moving venue.
Two price increases (about 15% in average price) may have cost buyers, but the effect is confounded with the venue change and untested. Peers also raised prices about 14%.

The organization lacks attribution and diagnostic data, so the board is reading a venue shock as a programming and marketing failure. Its evidence is anecdotal (emails, a press column) and ignores the confound.
Non-renewing the music director would put about $400k per season in grant money at risk. The key-person clause is Halvorsen $400k per season, and the New Works grant is $180k per season.
The hall reopening has slipped to September 2027, so the venue problem will last at least one more season, past the contract end date.

causalClaims.from: Venue relocation (distance, transit, parking, 40% fewer seats)
causalClaims.to: Single-ticket collapse and lapsed or non-attending subscribers
Evidence that repertoire drives the decline

actions.action: Do not base the December decision on the claim that her programming caused the 30% fall. Do not issue non-renewal notice on that ground.
actions.rationale: The evidence points to the venue, not repertoire, and non-renewal would put $400k per season of Halvorsen money (plus the New Works condition) at risk for no demonstrated revenue gain.

actions.action: Accept the cathedral's six 2026-27 dates and expand downtown or near-rail bookings where possible.
actions.rationale: Cathedral concerts sold about 48% more tickets and contributed about $31k more per concert than Brightwater.

actions.action: Reduce Brightwater access barriers: late shuttle from Central station, parking bundles or discounts, and a later bus. Plan for another season there, since reopening has slipped to September 2027.
actions.rationale: Travel, parking and safety are the top stated reasons for leaving, and 71% of lapsed patrons say they would likely return.

actions.action: Target lapsed subscribers and single-ticket buyers with win-back offers that tie into the downtown dates.
actions.rationale: The 0-2 attendance subscriber group renews at only 44%, and exit-survey respondents say they will return.

actions.action: Instrument marketing attribution (campaign, channel and ticket linkage) and review the agency arrangement. Do not judge marketing or the music director on it until the data exists.
actions.rationale: No one can currently show whether marketing is good or bad, and it reports to the Executive Director, not the music director.

actions.action: Handle the contract through a separate artistic and leadership evaluation. Renew or extend, or defer within the 31 December notice deadline, rather than treating revenue as the verdict.
actions.rationale: The revenue case against her is not made. Whether to renew should rest on artistic and governance criteria the board has not yet examined.

actions.action: Shift the programme back toward familiar classics to win back audience.
actions.rationale: Sales at Brightwater do not differ between concerts with and without major post-1945 works (E7), and only 12% of attenders who cut back cite programming (E8). A shift could also breach the 2-commission condition on the $180k grant.

actions.action: Cut prices or raise them further as the main fix.
actions.rationale: Price effects are confounded with the venue change; test them before changing prices.

actions.action: Launch a national search or fire the music director to signal action.
actions.rationale: It would treat a venue shock as a leadership failure and the real driver would remain.

nextEvidence: Per-concert sales and buyer mix controlling for venue, season and programme (including cathedral dates), plus a counterfactual estimate of what a peer-trend decline would have been without the move
Marketing attribution data (channel and campaign to ticket sales) and an external review of agency performance and reach in the Westmere market
Price-sensitivity evidence: single-ticket price tests or churn analysis by price band, separated from venue effects, plus lapsed-patron return behaviour at cathedral dates
output.summary: The 30% ticket-revenue fall is best explained by the forced move from a downtown, rail-adjacent 2,150-seat hall to a distant 1,290-seat venue. Revenue dropped in one step in 2023-24 and single-ticket sales fell 45%. Lapsed patrons and the survey cite travel and parking, and cathedral downtown concerts sell about 48% more. Programming does not predict sales at the same venue (E7) and is cited by about 11-12%. Marketing is untested, and it reports to the Executive Director, not the music director. Peers also fell about 29%, so some of the decline is regional. Non-renewal would put $400k per season of grant money at risk without addressing the cause. Fix access and venue, and measure marketing and pricing.
